title: Unchecked Safety Comment Invariant (Safety Theater)
pattern: Prose comments asserting crucial safety invariants or numerical bounds without any compiler-enforced types or runtime checks.
why_bad: Illusion of safety. If a caller violates the comment-only rule, the program suffers silent corruption or panic. Invariants must be enforced structurally or verified with assertions.
detection: Comments asserting safety limits (e.g. 'must not be zero', 'must be positive') on primitives where there are no compile-time type barriers or runtime `assert!` operations.
counterexample: The invariant enforced structurally (`NonZeroI32`) or mechanically (`assert!(count > 0)`) at function entry.
fix: Enforce the invariant with custom types (e.g., `NonZeroI32`) or add a mechanical `assert!` check at function entry.
source: Martin Fowler, *Refactoring* (2018), Chapter 3 ("Bad Smells in Code - Comments - Introduce Assertion").
